A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAPPIE research. The main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original Weibo and Twitter evaluations, component ablations, propagation-depth experiments and reader-feedback simulation results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds reader-scale experiments in Section 4.7, Figure 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The reader agents, TF-IDF top-k selection, role-aware multi-view graph learning and prediction objectives remain unchanged. Top-k selection already exists in v2; the revised k value is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chinese Weibo and English Twitter datasets for seven-category implicit emotion classification. Table 6 retains identical dataset statistics; varying k changes sampling within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators: KGAN, MMML, RDGCN, DAGCN, the GLM4/ChatGLM/Qwen baselines and their THOR/TOC combinations, and DeepSeek-R1. The case-study comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 Appendix B specifies top-100 selection. V3 Section 4.2 reports k=50 for Qwen on Weibo and k=100 for the other configurations. Section 4.7 also introduces evaluation at k=100, 50 and 25, while retaining the existing datasets, splits and metrics.

E4.justification: New Section 4.7 and Figure 4 test sensitivity to feedback-selection scale for both model variants and datasets, supported by expanded simulation counts in Table 3. The existing component-ablation questions, propagation-depth study and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The annotation-agreement figures in Appendix D are unchanged, and the new reader-scale plot adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes RAPPIE(Qwen) on Weibo from macro-F1/accuracy 0.433/0.566 to 0.500/0.608 under the revised k setting; all other Table 1 scores remain unchanged. Table 2 revises corresponding ablation scores and the stated maximum Weibo feedback-removal drop changes from 6.5 to 8.5 percentage points. Figure 4 and Table 3 add scale-dependent prediction and simulation results.

T1.justification: The problem definition, mathematical model and Equations (1)–(14) retain their substance. The added broadcasting and reader-scale explanations introduce no formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain PIEA, reader-feedback simulation, role-aware graph learning and two datasets. The claimed superiority over baselines and the conclusion's 17.4% and 6.5% macro-F1 improvements were already reported in v2.

C2.justification: V3 expands Section 4.5 with arguments about broadcasting despite missing follower links, equalizing reader-group sizes and limiting noisy-feedback effects. Section 4.7 adds a cost/diversity interpretation and an information-cocoon explanation for small reader groups. The LLM-bias limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-and-dataset repository statement and explicit per-configuration k values. Appendix D newly documents anonymization without establishing that the underlying datasets were revised, and the acknowledgements identify a data provider.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged. DeepSeek-R1 and the other comparison methods were already discussed and cited in v2.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgements and expands explanatory passages. The new reader-scale subsection shifts the case study from Section 4.7 to 4.8 without broadly restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: V3 restyles typography and labels in Figures 1–2, adds reader-scale Figure 4, expands Table 3 with top-k groups and relocates Table 2. Retained appendix figures are renumbered, with limited wording corrections in the case-study displays.

improvement.justification: The reader-scale study provides useful evidence about an existing configuration choice, while explicit k settings and code/data access information improve reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains: the revised Qwen-Weibo scores use a different setting, and the added claims about bias elimination and noisy-feedback suppression are not directly tested.
